items.headline: PM Wong says Singapore is ready to help the US verify how advanced chips are deployed here
items.summary: Speaking after the ASEAN Summit in Manila on Nov 17, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said Singapore would facilitate US checks on firms deploying advanced chips locally and called Washington's new export-licensing rule “manageable.” The rule, which covers chips bound for Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil, is tied to a US criminal probe into Singapore-based Megaspeed.

items.headline: More Singapore residents are both married and divorced than a decade ago, an MSF report finds
items.summary: A State of ASEAN Families Report 2026 coordinated by the Ministry of Social and Family Development found married people now make up 61.8% of Singapore's resident population, while the divorced-or-separated share rose to 4.2% from 3.8% in 2015. The median age of first marriage climbed to 29.6 for women and 31.1 for men.

items.headline: PM Wong to meet Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Nov 20 after the APEC leaders' meeting
items.summary: After attending the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong will hold a bilateral meeting with President Xi Jinping on Nov 20 before travelling to Beijing. In an APEC op-ed, Wong credited Lee Kuan Yew and Deng Xiaoping with laying the foundations for closer Singapore-China ties.

items.headline: Jurong West condo residents climbed stairs for five days after the block's only working lift kept failing
items.summary: Residents of the 14-storey Block 238 at Floravale in Jurong West were left using the stairs for five days when the building's sole operational lift repeatedly broke down; the second lift had been under modernisation since August. Management apologised, blamed ageing electronic components, and said the lift was restored on Nov 13.

items.headline: Singaporean man jailed 13 months for repeatedly crossing into Malaysia on his twin's passport
items.summary: Johnathan Yam Zhe Liang, 27, was sentenced on Nov 17 to 13 months and four weeks' jail after pleading guilty to four charges. After his own passport was impounded, he used his twin brother's passport to cross into Malaysia several times in early 2025, and was caught at Woodlands Checkpoint on Jan 22, 2025 when his biometrics failed to match.

items.headline: UK inflation climbs to a one-year high of 3.6% as record diesel prices bite
items.summary: Consumer prices rose 3.6% in the year to October, up from 3.5% in September and the highest reading in a year, driven by a 33% jump in motor-fuel costs and record diesel prices. Markets now price in roughly 80% odds of a quarter-point Bank of England rate rise in December.

items.headline: UK real wages fall for the first time since the 2023 cost-of-living crisis
items.summary: Official figures show regular pay adjusted for inflation fell 0.2% in the year to September — the first real-terms drop since May 2023 — as 3.5% nominal wage growth was outpaced by rising fuel and energy costs. The reversal undercuts the government's pledge to lift living standards.

items.headline: UK households face a 26% jump in energy bills in January, the steepest rise since 2022
items.summary: Analysts expect domestic energy bills to rise about 26% in January, the biggest increase since 2022, as conflict in the Middle East pushes up wholesale gas and electricity prices. The jump would add further strain to household budgets already squeezed by fuel costs.

items.headline: Commons passes the government's Immigration and Asylum Bill by 290 votes to 94
items.summary: The House of Commons passed the Immigration and Asylum Bill on Nov 17 by 290 votes to 94, avoiding a major backbench rebellion. The bill extends the settlement wait for about 500,000 migrants — most workers to 10 years and some small-boat arrivals up to 30 years, with a carve-out for care workers earning at least £25,000 — and now moves to the House of Lords.

items.headline: US and Venezuela sign a deal to restore military ties during Hegseth's visit to Caracas
items.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a new military partnership — covering joint training, intelligence sharing, and pooled equipment — on his first visit to Caracas since the January US operation that captured Nicolas Maduro, with acting President Delcy Rodriguez alongside him. Hegseth called the Maduro raid the most sophisticated military operation in Latin American history.

items.headline: Israel launches its first ground operation across Gaza's 'Yellow Line' since the ceasefire
items.summary: Israeli tanks advanced west of the Yellow Line into central Gaza near Salah al-Din Street, killing three Palestinians and forcing thousands to flee — the first such ground push since the October 2025 truce began. Israel said it targeted Hamas infrastructure amid claims the group is rearming, while Hamas called the move a flagrant violation of the ceasefire.

items.headline: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Kuwait and Bahrain intercept missiles and drones
items.summary: US fighter jets carried out what Washington called a self-defence strike on an Iranian missile-launch site on Qeshm Island after attacks on US personnel, and Iran retaliated against Gulf neighbours, with Kuwait and Bahrain saying they intercepted incoming missiles and drones. At least five ships were reportedly set ablaze by mines in the Strait of Hormuz as Oman and Qatar pressed for mediation.

items.headline: Xi tells APEC that China and Russia should lead the push to a multipolar world
items.summary: Meeting Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, President Xi Jinping said Beijing and Moscow should lead the shift to a “more fair and multipolar world order,” and Putin, treated as guest of honour, criticised economic coercion. Both pointed to a three-way summit with US President Donald Trump scheduled for Nov 19, the first-ever gathering of the three leaders.

items.headline: Rwanda-DRC peace process stalls as a new round of talks is set for Geneva
items.summary: The US-brokered Washington Accords between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda remain stuck on implementation, with another negotiating round expected in Geneva on Nov 19 as fighting between the M23 group and Congolese forces continues. Washington sanctioned Rwanda's Defence Ministry on Oct 28 over alleged M23 support, which Kigali denies, while a parallel Qatar-mediated track runs separately in Doha.

items.headline: Genesis AI raises $500M Series A to build dexterous robots
items.summary: Robotics startup Genesis AI announced a $500 million Series A led by Khosla Ventures, Premji Invest, and Eclipse to train dexterous robots using force data gathered from a sensor-equipped glove. The round is among the largest early-stage raises in robotics this year.

items.headline: Isomorphic Labs raises about $5B to push AI-designed drugs toward clinical trials
items.summary: The Google DeepMind drug-discovery spinout raised a Series C of roughly $5 billion, co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, as it moves toward taking its first AI-designed drug candidates into clinical trials. It is one of the largest funding rounds yet for AI in drug discovery.

items.headline: ByteDance nears a $500M deal to run OpenAI models on Microsoft Azure, irking OpenAI
items.summary: ByteDance is in advanced talks to spend roughly $500 million more on Microsoft Azure cloud services, largely to run OpenAI's models — a move The Information reports has upset OpenAI. The deal would deepen Microsoft's cloud ties with the owner of TikTok.

items.headline: SpaceX prepares a $40B debt sale to fund AI chip purchases
items.summary: SpaceX is set to begin part of a planned $40 billion debt sale to finance AI chip purchases, with roughly $4 billion of bonds potentially offered within days. The raise underscores how heavily the company is investing in computing for its Starlink and AI ambitions.

items.headline: India's Humyn Labs raises $47M to supply training data for US robotics
items.summary: India-based Humyn Labs raised $47 million in Series A financing, with Accel leading the equity portion, to supply training data to US AI and robotics companies. The deal highlights India's growing role in the global AI data-supply chain.

items.headline: Update: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, above range, ahead of a Thursday Nasdaq debut
items.summary: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, above the marketed $70-to-$78 range, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC. At 825 million shares the deal would raise about $68.5 billion, and trading is set to begin on the Nasdaq on Nov 19 under the ticker “ANT,” valuing the AI lab above the roughly $1.4 trillion it had targeted.

items.headline: Target beats on earnings as quarterly sales jump, and its shares rise about 7%
items.summary: Target reported adjusted earnings of $2.65 a share, well above the $2.07 expected, on revenue of $27.07 billion against a $26.56 billion estimate, with comparable sales up 5.6% versus a 3.8% forecast. It raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to between $10.65 and $11.40, and the stock rose about 7%.

items.headline: Nvidia's post-earnings gains evaporate as the S&P 500 slips below its 200-day average
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell below its 200-day moving average on Nov 18 as Nvidia swung from above $164 overnight to below $152, ending about 2.9% lower despite beating revenue and guidance estimates. Metals also sold off, with copper futures down about 5% to their lowest since April, as traders braced for Anthropic's Nasdaq debut.

items.headline: US Treasury yields ease after Fed minutes and Waller's remarks temper rate-cut bets
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield fell more than four basis points to about 5.06% and the 30-year to roughly 5.41% as investors digested the latest Federal Reserve minutes and comments from Governor Christopher Waller. The move partly unwound a recent climb driven by fading expectations of a December cut.

items.headline: 🎾 Alcaraz beats Medvedev to move to the brink of the Turin semi-finals
items.summary: Carlos Alcaraz beat Daniil Medvedev 6-2, 6-4 on Nov 18 to stay unbeaten in his ATP Finals group despite a leg issue, moving to the verge of a semi-final place. His qualification was sealed when Frances Tiafoe took a set off Flavio Cobolli later in the day.

items.headline: 🎾 Arevalo and Pavic upset the defending champions to reach the Turin doubles semis
items.summary: Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic beat defending champions and newly crowned year-end No. 1s Harri Heliovaara and Henry Patten 6-7(5), 6-3, 10-4 on Nov 17 to reach the ATP Finals doubles semi-finals. The result left the top seeds needing to win their final group match to advance.

items.headline: 🏏 India open their New Zealand tour as the first Test begins in Wellington
items.summary: India, captained by Shubman Gill with KL Rahul as his deputy, start their series against New Zealand in the first Test at Wellington from Nov 19, with Rishabh Pant cleared to keep wicket and Jasprit Bumrah leading the attack. New Zealand, led by Tom Latham, are without the injured Mitchell Santner, pushing Glenn Phillips into the spin-allrounder role.

items.headline: 🏎️ Cadillac confirms Bottas alongside Perez for its 2027 Formula 1 line-up
items.summary: Cadillac confirmed on Nov 18, on the eve of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, that Valtteri Bottas will stay with the team for 2027 after deciding against fast-tracking American test driver Colton Herta. He partners Sergio Perez, who has signed a contract running to the end of 2029.

items.headline: 🏎️ Mercedes bring an upgraded turbo to Las Vegas as Wolff hints he may back Russell
items.summary: Mercedes confirmed their ADUO turbo upgrade is ready for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, with Kimi Antonelli set to run the new engine part while George Russell keeps his current unit to protect his grid position. Team principal Toto Wolff said Mercedes could prioritise Russell over the final three rounds, with Verstappen on 279 points leading Russell on 262 and Hamilton on 261 in the fight for second.

items.headline: Voyager 1 becomes the first spacecraft to reach one light-day from Earth
items.summary: NASA said Voyager 1 passed one light-day from Earth — about 16 billion miles — at 5:16 a.m. EST on Nov 18, 2026, 49 years after its launch and the first human-made object to do so. A command now takes a full day to reach the probe, and its reply a further day to return.

items.headline: Stratospheric dust grains carry a chemical fingerprint of ancient ice beyond Neptune
items.summary: NASA Johnson Space Center scientists led by Lindsay Keller analysed 12 interplanetary dust particles collected by a high-altitude ER-2 aircraft and found oxygen-isotope signatures of water that once reacted with rock in the Kuiper Belt. The result implies liquid water existed beyond Neptune in the early solar system.

items.headline: A Neanderthal DNA segment is linked to lower schizophrenia risk in modern humans
items.summary: A study in PNAS using UK Biobank data reports that people carrying two copies of a Neanderthal-derived segment near the gene DAAM1 have a nearly 10% lower risk of schizophrenia, alongside a slightly smaller visual-processing region of the brain. The finding adds to evidence that archaic DNA still shapes human health.

items.headline: NASA will end its 26-year Terra Earth-observing mission
items.summary: NASA announced that Terra, launched in 1999 and a workhorse for climate, wildfire, and land-cover data, will stop collecting science data on Dec 1, 2026, with a full power-down planned for January 2027. The satellite long outlasted its original six-year design life.

items.headline: A new study warns SpaceX's planned orbital data centres could sharply worsen upper-atmosphere pollution
items.summary: A modelling study finds that SpaceX's proposed fleet of roughly one million orbital data-centre satellites could raise some forms of upper-atmosphere pollution more than a hundredfold. The authors could not quantify metal pollution because the satellites' materials are undisclosed.

fun_fact.headline: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood
fun_fact.body: An octopus has three hearts and blue, copper-based blood. Two branchial hearts pump blood through the gills, while a third systemic heart drives it around the rest of the body — and that systemic heart pauses during jet-propelled swimming, which is one reason octopuses often prefer to crawl.

puzzle.title: Crossing in the Dark
puzzle.body:
Four hikers must cross a rickety footbridge at night. They have one torch, the bridge holds at most two people at a time, and whoever crosses must carry the torch, so it has to be walked back for the others.
They walk at different speeds, and a pair moves at the slower person's pace: Ann takes 1 minute, Ben 2 minutes, Cara 5 minutes, and Dan 10 minutes.
What is the least total time in which all four get across?
puzzle.approach: The fastest hiker escorting everyone looks efficient — but check whether sending your two slowest travellers across together saves more time.
puzzle.answer:
17 minutes.
The key is to send the two slowest together so Dan's 10 minutes and Cara's 5 overlap in a single trip.
1) Ann + Ben cross together, 2 min (total 2)
2) Ann returns with the torch, 1 min (total 3)
3) Cara + Dan cross together, 10 min (total 13)
4) Ben returns with the torch, 2 min (total 15)
5) Ann + Ben cross together, 2 min (total 17)
Having fast Ann escort each person instead costs 10 + 1 + 5 + 1 + 2 = 19 minutes, so 17 is optimal.

word_puzzle.title: Worth Noting
word_puzzle.body:
Centre letter: T  (must appear in every word)
Outer letters:  A · B · E · L · N · O

Build as many words as you can of 4+ letters, each containing T, using only these seven letters (letters may repeat). Exactly one word — the pangram — uses all seven.
Target: find the pangram plus a dozen more.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word must use the centre letter T and only the seven letters shown; letters may repeat. One word — the pangram — uses all seven.
word_puzzle.answer:
Pangram: NOTABLE  (uses A, B, E, L, N, O, T).
Other valid words (4+ letters, each containing T):
ABLATE · ANTE · ATONE · BATON · BEATEN · BLOAT · BOTTLE · LATTE · NOTATE · NOTE · OBLATE · TABLE · TABLET · TABOO · TALENT · TALON · TONE · TOTAL
Every word uses only the letters A, B, E, L, N, O, T.
